observation.visible_scene: Night sky densely filled with the lingering curved trails of a large firework display (willow/palm type) in red, white-green and purple-blue, interwoven with several soft grayish smoke puffs. The trail network and smoke occupy the whole frame throughout the excerpt and slowly diffuse/dim. Multiple small secondary bursts pop and expand within this field.
visible_changes: A broad pinkish glowing burst sits left-of-center from the first frame and persists, slowly fading and shifting slightly relative to the frame edges.
Around t=0.5–0.75s a yellow-white starburst appears at center-right, radiates outward (expansion), then fades into the surrounding trails.
Around t=1.25s a brief bright white flash with short purple streaks appears at center and dissipates.
Around t=1.5–1.75s small white star-shaped bursts appear at upper-right and at left-center, then vanish.
Around t=2.08–2.4s a bright starburst ignites at center, expands into a larger radiating pink/white burst, then fades to a diffuse pink glow by t=3.0s.
Around t=2.83–3.1s another starburst forms lower-center, expands, and fades.
The overall curved-trail pattern and smoke clouds drift slowly and lose brightness across the clip; individual spark points along trails shift downward over time.
outside_clip_unknowns: What launched or caused the bursts; the full firework sequence before the crop and after the last frame; the ground, horizon, or any observer/launcher.
Whether the bright starbursts are separate physical explosions or transient camera/lens effects cannot be confirmed beyond their visible appearance.
uncertain_details: Whether the slow shift of the trail network relative to the frame edges is camera drift/pan or the physical descent of the trails; background evidence is insufficient to separate the two.
Exact count and boundaries of distinct bursts, since some merge with the dense trail field; brightness changes (dimming vs. new ignition) are partly ambiguous against the busy background.
